- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); cap forecast rise after spike to 2–4% max.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → -0.67 → 0.67), model misreads momentum; apply smoothing filter to sentiment-weighted average before forecasting.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.33); model tends to overcommit; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent mean.
